body:
## Purpose

This PR follows up on #2634 by reducing the compiler work for operator broadcasts, and by sharing more array access code from `DataLayouts` between CPUs and GPUs. Several CPU slow paths have been eliminated: fills and simple pointwise operations dominated by array indexing, and stencil operations on orthonormal vectors, are now more than 10x faster in some cases.

## Disclosure

This PR and its description were mostly generated using Claude.

## Content

- Reduce operator latency
  - Avoid error messages that interpolate types at runtime, which CUDA v6 inlines into kernels that reach them.
    - Replace `fieldname` with `Base.fieldindex`.
    - Replace `unrolled_map` over more than one `NamedTuple` with `map` to avoid `output_promote_result` (this needs to be fixed upstream).
  - Internal rebuilds that are valid by construction do not compile size checks (`rebuild`/`reinterpret` still check).
  - Point views located by dividing a linear index hide their constant strides from inference (`Base.compilerbarrier`).
  - Operator broadcasts directly compare slice indices with `===`.
  - GPU kernels reuse the slice subscope computed on the host.
  - Stencil point updates are inferred without constant propagation.
  - MatrixFields band products evaluate their rows directly in `stencil_value`.
  - The `inline_apply_operators` and one-argument `pointwise_stencil` forwarding layers are removed.
  - Pairwise reductions are compiled once per type instead of being inlined into every caller.
    - `unit_mapreduce.jl` compiles about 2x faster.
- Unify CPU/GPU array access
  - Points in CPU `Array`s use the same alternative to `SubArray` as GPU kernels (`DataLayouts.PointView`).
  - Struct values are read and written at a linear index and stride (`Utilities.linear_index_and_stride`).
  - All unmasked point loops use linear indices when every argument supports them, except over layouts with only static sizes, several axes longer than 1, and an axis whose length is not a power of two (on `main`, only kernel-wide GPU loops used linear indices, even over such layouts).
    - Layouts with several components reach `IndexLinear` parent arrays with only one division per point.
    - Linear indices are responsible for most of this PR's speedup for pointwise CPU broadcasts constructed and materialized in the same function.
    - Calls to `fill!` on layouts with dynamic sizes are up to 8x faster on CPUs.
  - LLVM assumes that parent arrays have the extents fixed by their layout's type (`DataLayouts.assume_extents`).
    - Parent array size checks are no longer needed in `broadcastable`.
    - On CPUs, a broadcast whose `materialize!` is compiled separately from its constructor keeps constant strides, exactly like one compiled with its constructor (on `main`, it was about 3x slower).
    - Calls to `fill!` on layouts with fully inferred sizes are up to 34x faster on CPUs.
- Other optimizations
  - Masked GPU point loops, limiter kernels, and DG kernels skip bounds checks and use 32-bit index arithmetic.
  - Host-side `Grids.LevelGrid` construction checks the level, so local geometry reads can skip bounds checks.
  - Operator broadcast constructors and most `Field` broadcast space checks are inlined, speeding up CPU stencils.
  - The method of `inv` for 2-tensors is inlined, speeding up CPU stencils that convert orthonormal vectors.
  - Sums and products inline their point reads, speeding up multi-component sums on CPUs.
    - Scalar field sums are around 10% faster, but `Covariant12Vector` sums are 5x faster.
    - Single-threaded sums/products can differ in the last bits, as `@simd` now reassociates their inlined reads.
- Bug fixes
  - Instead of returning invalid results, `similar(data, dims)` with mismatched `dims`, `Spaces.level` with an out-of-range level, and out-of-range `Perimeter2D` indexing now throw.
  - Multi-element tuple broadcasts into `DataLayout`s index correctly on GPUs.
  - Point loops with mixed `Field` and `DataLayout` arguments no longer error on GPUs.
  - GPU kernels support at most `2^31 − 1` elements per array (same limit as for slices in `foreach_slice`).
    - `LLVM.jl` can sign-extend 32-bit indices, so the old `2^32 − 1` limit could permit wrong array addresses.
- Remove outdated code
  - Drop `cart_ind`/`linear_ind` in Utilities, and drop `kernel_indexes`/`valid_range` in the CUDA extension.
  - Drop an unreachable method of `subscope_indices` and several unused `CompactDeviceView` methods.
  - Drop the `(-1, -1)` sentinel and the zero-argument `getindex` method of `Perimeter2D`.

## Comparison against main

Each row compares this PR ([8088](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/8088), [478](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/478), [569](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/569)) with `main` ([8078](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/8078), [451](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/451), [556](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/556)). Each row covers the jobs or benchmark cases that passed in both builds on the same CPU node type and GPU model, and rows over several of them give the min / median / max of the PR values, the `main` values, and the per-job ratios. Wall-time rows only include jobs that took at least a minute in both builds.

title: Reduce operator latency and optimize CPU array views
